scenes.text: There is a planet that spins on its side, like a rolling ball.
It's Uranus, and it's tipped over by almost ninety eight degrees.
Earth, for comparison, is tilted only about twenty three and a half degrees.
One trip around the Sun takes Uranus about eighty four Earth years.
Because it's sideways, almost a whole half of the planet can stay in sunlight for years.
Meanwhile, the other half sits in nonstop darkness.
Yet a single spin, one Uranus day, takes only about seventeen hours.
Most astronomers suspect a huge icy object, about the size of Earth, knocked it over long ago.
It can get as cold as minus three hundred seventy one degrees Fahrenheit there.
A little methane in its air gives it that blue color.
When William Herschel found it in seventeen eighty one, he first thought it was a comet.
Its moons are named after characters from Shakespeare and Alexander Pope.
Only one spacecraft has ever visited: Voyager two, in January nineteen eighty six.
It flew within about fifty thousand miles of the cloud tops.
Would you rather live with sideways seasons, or keep ours?

title: The planet that spins on its side 🪐
caption: Uranus is tilted about 98 degrees, so it rolls around the Sun on its side. One year there lasts about 84 Earth years.
